# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 80 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 80 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_080_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Chapter 3

**1** He showed me many other trees, some budding and some withered. **2** And he said to me, "Do you see these trees?" "I see them, Lord," I replied. "Those that are budding and sprouting," he said, "are those who are about to repent and live; for the Lord, seeing their repentance, judged it good to grant life to them. **3** But those that are withered and bear no fruit are those who have apostatized in their hearts and will not return to repentance, nor will they return among the living." **4** I said to him, "Lord, why then did you bring some of the withered ones among those who repented?" He answered me, "So that, beholding the joyful appearance of those who are repenting, they might be put to shame and themselves repent. For if they see the glory of those who repented — and knew not the Lord before, but now know him — they will repent with all their heart." **5** "But if they do not repent, Lord," I said, "what will become of them?" "They shall die," he said — "those who do not repent at that point. But those who repented and lived righteously shall live unto God. But those who did not repent and persisted in their wicked deeds shall die." **6** I asked, "But those who returned the rod entirely green and cracked — who are they?" He said to me, "They were always faithful and good, but they harbored jealousy toward one another over questions of pre-eminence and some glory. But they are all foolish in having such jealousy among themselves over pre-eminence." **7** "And those who returned their rods half-withered and cracked — who are these?" I asked. **8** "These are those who were faithful but became rich and acquired reputation among the Gentiles. They clothed themselves in great pride and became arrogant, and abandoned the truth, and did not attach themselves to the righteous but lived with the Gentiles, and this way of life appeared better to them. Yet they did not depart from God but remained in the faith, though they did not perform the works of faith. **9** Many of them repented, but some continued in their deeds. These received their rods retaining sap, for they did not depart from the living God, nor did the name depart from their lips. These therefore received their rods with sap remaining."

---

*LOGOS preserves the formal structure of the moral distinctions. "Clothed themselves in great pride" renders the Greek endusanto megalēn huperēphanían.*
